Package com.egradx.auth.dto

Record Class EgradxAuthResult

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Record
com.egradx.auth.dto.EgradxAuthResult
Record Components:
organizationId - the organization this session is scoped to, or null if the user belongs to none yet
platformOrganization - whether organizationId is the platform organization — i.e. whether this session administers the platform rather than one tenant. Informational: a client should still gate its screens on authorities, which is what the server actually enforces.
roleId - the role held in organizationId, or null if the user has no role there yet
roleName - that role's display name — included so a client can render "signed in as Admin" without a second round trip
organizationName - the name of organizationId, so a client can say which organization the session is in without a second call; null with no organization
public record EgradxAuthResult(String accessToken, String refreshToken, String tokenType, Instant expiresAt, EgradxUserDto user, UUID organizationId, boolean platformOrganization, UUID roleId, String roleName, Set<String> authorities, String organizationName) extends Record
Result of a successful login: a bearer access token, an opaque refresh token, the organization the access token is scoped to, the role held there, and the flat set of granular authority names that role resolves to at the moment of login only — a snapshot for immediate UI use, not authoritative for anything after that moment. Every request after this one has its authorities re-resolved fresh (see EgradxPermissionResolver), so a role edit takes effect on the very next request, not the next login.
